name: Arm Cortex 10-pin (CoreSight 10)
mates: A JTAG or SWD probe's 10-way 1.27 mm (0.05 in) ribbon cable, into the CoreSight 10 (Cortex Debug) header on the target, typically a Samtec FTSH-105 style 2×5 header.
numbering: Pins 1 to 10 as on a 2-row header: odd pins in one row, even pins in the other, pin 1 at one end. Pin 7 is the key position and must not be fitted on the target connector. Arm's text gives only the table (the figure is an image); the 1.27 mm pitch and FTSH-105 style are from Tag-Connect's TC2030-CTX datasheet, not from these Arm pages. Tag-Connect's TC2050 footprint numbers the same signals differently (see tc2050-swd).

source.title: Arm DS-5 Arm DSTREAM System and Interface Design Reference Guide, version 5.29: CoreSight 10 pinouts, Table 2-12 CoreSight 10 interface pinout table, and Table 2-13 CoreSight 10 signals (web edition, no page numbers)

pins.note: Table 2-13: supplies the probe with the target's debug rail voltage to match its I/O levels. It can be tied high on the target; if pulled high by a resistor, the resistor must be no greater than 100 Ω.
Table 2-13 advises series-terminating SWDIO close to the target processor.
Table 2-13 advises series-terminating SWO and TDO close to the target processor.
Table 2-13: this pin must not be present on the target connector. ST's STDC14 (pin 9) and Tag-Connect's TC2030-CTX and TC2050-ARM2010 datasheets put RTCK at this position instead.
JTAG only; not used in SWD mode.
ST (STDC14 pin 11) and Tag-Connect call this position GNDDetect.
Table 2-13: system reset, driven by the probe or the target; typically pulled high on the target.
